guarantees.claim: sync_err_q is cleared to 0 when rst_ni is low.
sync_err_q is cleared to 0 when op_done_i is high (and rst_ni high).
When op_done_i is low and op_update_i is high, sync_err_q is updated with the current value of sync_err_d.
When rst_ni is high and neither op_done_i nor op_update_i is asserted, sync_err_q retains its previous value.

assumptions.claim: sync_err_d must be stable and valid at the rising clock edge when op_update_i is asserted.
assumptions.risk: If sync_err_d changes coincident with the update pulse, sync_err_q may capture a metastable or incorrect value.

uncertain_points.claim: The priority of op_done_i over op_update_i may cause loss of a new error assertion when an operation completes simultaneously.
uncertain_points.cond: op_done_i and op_update_i both high in the same cycle
uncertain_points.risk: A valid synchronous error (sync_err_d) could be cleared before the error is processed or logged, leading to undetected faults.

uncertain_points.claim: If op_done_i remains asserted for multiple cycles, any op_update_i during that window is ignored, suppressing error capture.
uncertain_points.cond: op_done_i = 1 for two or more consecutive cycles
uncertain_points.risk: Errors occurring while an operation is marked done may be silently discarded, weakening fault detection during operation tails.

uncertain_points.claim: The mutual exclusion or pulse width of op_done_i and op_update_i is not locally enforced; the behavior relies on external control logic.
uncertain_points.cond: External generation of op_done_i and op_update_i
uncertain_points.risk: If the external protocol allows overlapping or long-lasting assertions, error clearing/update semantics become ambiguous.
